title: A ramp that reaches 5 V in about a millisecond
story: An inverting integrator turns a constant -1 V input into a steadily rising ramp: the 10 kOhm input resistor feeds a constant current into the feedback capacitor. A timing circuit downstream fires when the ramp crosses 5 V, and it must fire about 1 ms after the start. Choose the feedback capacitor (it starts empty).

goals.label: ramp crosses 5 V between 0.9 and 1.3 ms
ramp is straight: about half way (2.0-2.6 V) at 0.5 ms

hints: The minus input is a virtual ground, so the input current is 1 V / 10 kOhm = 100 uA, all of it into the capacitor.
A capacitor charged by a constant current I rises at I / C volts per second.
To reach 5 V in 1 ms you need 5000 V/s: C = 100 uA / 5000 V/s.
